name: Cabernet Sauvignon
description: The undisputed king of red wines, producing full-bodied wines with blackcurrant, cedar, and spice notes. It thrives in warm climates and forms the backbone of Bordeaux's legendary blends.

name: Pinot Noir
description: Known as the heartbreak grape for its difficulty to grow, it produces elegant wines with cherry and earthy notes. This thin-skinned variety expresses terroir like no other grape.

name: Chardonnay
description: The world's most versatile white grape, acting as a canvas for winemakers to craft everything from crisp to buttery styles. It responds beautifully to oak aging and malolactic fermentation.

name: Merlot
description: A soft and velvety red grape that produces approachable wines with plum and chocolate flavors. It serves as an excellent blending partner and stands beautifully on its own.

name: Syrah
description: A powerful grape producing intense wines with pepper, smoke, and dark fruit characteristics. Known as Syrah in France and Shiraz in Australia, it adapts dramatically to its climate.

name: Sauvignon Blanc
description: A zesty and herbaceous white grape known for its crisp acidity and distinctive citrus and green notes. It expresses vastly different characters from the Loire Valley to New Zealand.

name: Riesling
description: An aromatic white grape with exceptional purity and high acidity that ages remarkably well. It ranges from bone-dry to lusciously sweet, developing complex petrol notes with age.

name: Nebbiolo
description: A legendary Italian grape producing pale-colored wines with massive tannins and floral aromas of tar and roses. It requires long aging to soften and is the soul of Barolo and Barbaresco.

name: Sangiovese
description: Italy's most planted red grape, producing savory wines with vibrant cherry and tomato leaf characters. It is the backbone of Chianti, Brunello di Montalcino, and countless Tuscan wines.

name: Grenache
description: A sweet red fruit-driven grape that produces wines high in alcohol with strawberry and raspberry flavors. It is a key component in Southern Rhône blends and Spanish Garnacha wines.

name: Tempranillo
description: Spain's noble grape variety, producing elegant wines with leather, tobacco, and red berry notes. It is the backbone of Rioja and Ribera del Duero, aging beautifully in American oak.

name: Malbec
description: Originally from Cahors, France, this dark and inky grape has become Argentina's signature variety. It produces velvety wines with intense plum, blueberry, and cocoa flavors.

name: Cabernet Franc
description: The parent grape of Cabernet Sauvignon, known for its herbaceous character with bell pepper and raspberry notes. It excels in the Loire Valley and plays a supporting role in Bordeaux blends.

name: Chenin Blanc
description: An incredibly versatile chameleon grape capable of producing dry, sweet, and sparkling wines. Its high acidity allows for exceptional aging and expression of terroir.

name: Viognier
description: A perfumed and aromatic white grape producing full-bodied wines with peach, tangerine, and honeysuckle notes. It originates from the Rhône Valley and is often co-fermented with Syrah.

name: Gamay
description: A fruity and fresh grape that produces light, gulpable wines perfect for serving slightly chilled. It is the sole grape of Beaujolais and excels with carbonic maceration techniques.

name: Zinfandel
description: A bold and jammy grape that produces high-alcohol wines with ripe berry and spice characteristics. Genetically identical to Primitivo, it has become California's signature red variety.

name: Semillon
description: A golden-hued grape often blended with Sauvignon Blanc, producing waxy whites with lemon curd and lanolin notes. It is essential for Sauternes and ages remarkably well.

name: Mourvèdre
description: A meaty and herbal red grape that produces full-bodied wines with game, black fruit, and herb flavors. It is a key blending partner in GSM blends and the star of Bandol rosé.

name: Barbera
description: A juicy and high-acid Italian grape that produces everyday drinking wines with sour cherry and herb flavors. It thrives in Piedmont and offers excellent value.

name: Pinot Gris
description: A mutation of Pinot Noir that produces white wines ranging from zesty Italian Pinot Grigio to rich Alsatian styles. Its grayish-pink skin gives it its name.

name: Petit Verdot
description: A late-ripening Bordeaux blending grape that adds violet aromas and deep color to wines. Rarely bottled alone, it provides structure and inky depth to the final blend.

name: Carmenère
description: Once thought extinct in Bordeaux, this lost grape found a new home in Chile where it produces distinctive wines. Its green pepper and raspberry notes make it Chile's signature variety.

name: Torrontés
description: Argentina's signature white grape that smells sweet but tastes dry, often deceiving the senses. Its intense rose and lychee aromas make it one of the world's most distinctive whites.

name: Moscato
description: One of the world's oldest grape families, known for its sweet, fizzy, and intensely aromatic wines. Its orange blossom perfume and low alcohol make it perfect for casual sipping.

name: Gewürztraminer
description: A highly aromatic grape with distinctive lychee and rose petal aromas that is unmistakable in blind tastings. Its name means 'spiced traminer' and it produces rich wines with low acidity.

name: Albariño
description: Spain's coastal Atlantic white grape that produces crisp, refreshing wines with apricot and sea salt notes. It thrives in Rías Baixas where ocean influence creates distinctive saline character.

name: Grüner Veltliner
description: Austria's pride and most planted grape, known for its distinctive white pepper and green pea notes. It ranges from light and crisp to powerful and age-worthy depending on terroir.

name: Vermentino
description: A Mediterranean white grape that thrives along coastal regions, producing citrus-driven wines with herbal hints. It is known by different names across Sardinia, Corsica, and the French Riviera.

name: Verdejo
description: An aromatic Spanish white grape that produces herbal wines with fennel and grapefruit characteristics. It is the star of Rueda and offers a Spanish alternative to Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Roussanne
description: A golden Rhône white grape that produces full-bodied wines with herbal tea and pear flavors. It is often blended with Marsanne and ages beautifully, developing honeyed complexity.

name: Marsanne
description: A rich white Rhône grape that produces nutty, full-bodied wines with almond and marzipan notes. It develops waxy, honeyed flavors with age and pairs beautifully with rich dishes.

name: Trebbiano
description: A light and neutral Italian workhorse grape that produces high-volume, everyday white wines. It forms the base of many Italian wines and French Cognac production.

name: Fiano
description: An aromatic Italian white grape from Campania that produces wines with hazelnut and honey notes. It has ancient origins and is experiencing a modern renaissance.

name: Assyrtiko
description: A Greek grape from Santorini with intense mineral character and very high acidity. It thrives on volcanic soils and produces wines with remarkable saline and citrus notes.

name: Aglianico
description: A powerful Italian red grape from southern Italy producing tannic, age-worthy wines with plum and leather notes. It is often called the 'Barolo of the South'.

name: Nero d'Avola
description: Sicily's most important red grape, producing rich wines with black cherry, plum, and spice flavors. It has become the ambassador of Sicilian winemaking.

name: Touriga Nacional
description: Portugal's noblest grape and the backbone of Port wine, producing intensely colored wines with violet and dark fruit notes. It excels in both fortified and dry table wines.

name: Tannat
description: A tannic powerhouse grape that has become Uruguay's national variety. It produces deeply colored, robust wines with blackberry and leather characteristics.

name: Furmint
description: The primary grape of Hungary's famous Tokaji sweet wines with very high acidity and citrus notes. It also makes excellent dry wines with smoky, minerally complexity.

name: Marselan
description: A Cabernet Sauvignon and Grenache crossing that has become the flagship red of modern China. Produces plush, dark-fruited wines with polished tannins in the foothills of Helan Mountain.

name: Cabernet Gernischt
description: A historic Bordeaux transplant thriving in China, often mistaken for Carmenère. Shows herbal spice and black fruit with a distinctly savory edge in cooler Chinese vineyards.

name: Koshu
description: Japan's signature pale-purple skinned grape that yields delicate, mineral-driven whites. Its subtle citrus and jasmine notes shine in the misty foothills of Mount Fuji.

name: Muscat Bailey A
description: A hybrid created in Japan combining Muscat of Hamburg and Bailey, producing aromatic, softly tannic reds with strawberry candy notes. Often vinified as a chilled, vibrant style.

name: Saperavi
description: Georgia's flagship teinturier red with intense black fruit, savory spice, and the structure to age gracefully.

name: Rkatsiteli
description: Ancient Georgian white grape famed for amber qvevri wines with quince, tea, and honeyed depth.

name: Kisi
description: Fragrant Georgian white offering apricot, white flowers, and subtle tannin when fermented on skins.

name: Dolcetto
description: A Piedmontese red grape known for juicy black fruit, low acidity, and soft tannins, making it ideal for early drinking. Despite the name meaning 'little sweet one,' the wines are typically dry and pleasantly bitter on the finish.

name: Pinotage
description: South Africa's signature crossing of Pinot Noir and Cinsault, producing deeply colored wines with dark berry fruit, smoke, and earthy spice. Styles range from fresh and fruit-driven to concentrated, oak-aged bottlings.

name: Montepulciano
description: A widely planted central Italian red grape that gives plush, fruit-forward wines with moderate tannin and herbal depth. It is the backbone of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo and responds well to both youthful and oak-aged styles.

name: Corvina
description: The principal red grape of Valpolicella, prized for sour-cherry brightness and herbal lift. Its thick skins and naturally high acidity make it especially suited to appassimento styles like Amarone.

name: Rondinella
description: A reliable blending grape from Veneto commonly paired with Corvina in Valpolicella and Amarone. It contributes color, floral aromatics, and steady acidity, especially in dried-grape wines.

name: Pinot Blanc
description: A white mutation of Pinot Noir producing crisp wines with orchard fruit, almond, and gentle floral notes. It shines in Alsace, Alto Adige, and Germany, where styles range from fresh and linear to richer, lees-aged expressions.

name: Pinot Meunier
description: A key Champagne grape that brings ripe fruit, approachability, and early charm to sparkling blends. As a still wine it can show bright red berry flavors, supple texture, and moderate structure.

name: Petite Sirah
description: A deeply colored, full-bodied red grape known for bold blackberry fruit, pepper, and firm tannins. Widely planted in California, it produces structured wines that can age well with oak integration.

name: Palomino
description: The principal white grape of Jerez, valued for its neutral profile and ability to transmit the effects of biological and oxidative aging in Sherry. In warm climates it yields dry wines with subtle orchard fruit, almond, and saline notes.

name: Baga
description: Portugal's structured red grape from Bairrada, producing high-acid, high-tannin wines with dark berries, tobacco, and earthy complexity. It can be rustic in youth but rewards aging and careful extraction.

name: Teroldego
description: An alpine red from Trentino known for vivid color, dark berry fruit, and firm but polished tannins. It combines mountain freshness with savory spice and often performs well in both stainless and oak-aged styles.

name: Lagrein
description: A deeply pigmented grape from Alto Adige producing structured wines with blackberry, cocoa, and smoky spice. It can be intensely tannic when young, then evolves toward velvety, savory complexity.

name: Aligoté
description: Burgundy's bright, high-acid white grape offering lemon, green apple, and chalky mineral notes. Traditionally used in Kir and increasingly bottled as serious single-varietal wines from cooler limestone sites.

name: Melon de Bourgogne
description: The grape behind Muscadet, the Loire's seafood white — every bottle of Muscadet is Melon de Bourgogne. It delivers lean, saline whites with citrus zest and subtle yeasty notes when aged on lees, and its neutral profile and brisk acidity make it especially seafood-friendly.

name: Xinomavro
description: Greece's age-worthy northern red known for high acidity, firm tannins, and aromas of sour cherry, olive, and sun-dried tomato. Often compared stylistically to Nebbiolo for its structure and savory complexity.

name: Agiorgitiko
description: A versatile Greek red from Nemea producing plush wines with red berry fruit, warm spice, and supple tannins. Depending on altitude and élevage, styles range from juicy and youthful to rich and oak-influenced.

name: Glera
description: The principal grape of Prosecco, prized for fresh pear, apple, and white blossom aromas with lively but gentle acidity. It is typically crafted in tank-method sparkling wines that emphasize bright fruit and approachability.

name: Carignan
description: A Mediterranean red grape known for deep color, savory dark fruit, and naturally high acidity. Old-vine plantings in southern France and Spain can produce concentrated, mineral wines with notable structure.

name: Cinsault
description: A soft, aromatic red grape prized for red-fruit perfume and supple tannins. Often used in Rhône and southern French blends, it is also central to many pale, delicate rosé wines.

name: Falanghina
description: A southern Italian white grape delivering bright citrus, apple, and floral aromas with refreshing acidity. It has become a flagship variety in Campania for both crisp young and textured styles.

name: Verdicchio
description: A classic central Italian white grape known for citrus zest, bitter-almond finish, and subtle saline minerality. It balances freshness and texture, with top bottlings capable of significant aging.

name: Müller-Thurgau
description: A crossing of Riesling and Madeleine Royale that produces aromatic, easy-drinking whites with gentle acidity. Styles often show orchard fruit, fresh herbs, and soft floral notes.

name: Silvaner
description: A traditional Central European white grape offering understated aromatics, savory texture, and marked site expression. In Franconia and Alsace it can produce dry wines with herbal, orchard, and stony nuances.

name: Godello
description: A rising Spanish white grape from Galicia and Bierzo with citrus, orchard fruit, and mineral depth. It can be vinified in fresh steel styles or richer barrel-aged expressions with notable complexity.

name: Verdelho
description: A versatile white grape associated with Madeira and Australian coastal regions, showing tropical citrus, herbal hints, and bright freshness. It can produce both dry table wines and fortified expressions.

name: Arinto
description: A Portuguese white grape prized for naturally high acidity and citrus-mineral precision, even in warm climates. It forms the backbone of many fresh Atlantic whites and ages gracefully with bottle time.

name: Zweigelt
description: Austria's most planted red grape, combining juicy cherry fruit with peppery spice and bright acidity. It can range from fresh, everyday bottlings to more structured oak-aged versions.

name: Blaufränkisch
description: A central European red grape known for vivid acidity, dark berry fruit, and spicy, mineral edge. It produces energetic wines that can show excellent aging potential in cooler sites.

name: Nerello Mascalese
description: Sicily's Etna flagship red, delivering pale color but firm structure with red fruit, herbs, and volcanic minerality. Often compared to Pinot Noir or Nebbiolo for its aromatic lift and tension.

name: Primitivo
description: A warm-climate red grape known for ripe black fruit, jammy richness, and generous alcohol. In Puglia it produces plush, spicy wines and shares a genetic identity with Zinfandel.

name: Friulano
description: A northeastern Italian white grape with citrus, almond, and subtle herbal notes, often textured and dry. It is a benchmark variety of Friuli with notable food-pairing versatility.

name: Fer Servadou
description: A southwest French red grape valued for brisk acidity, black fruit, and peppery herbal character. It adds structure and freshness in blends and can produce savory, medium-bodied varietal wines.

name: Moschofilero
description: An aromatic Greek pink-skinned grape used for fragrant white wines with rose, citrus, and spice notes. It is especially associated with high-altitude Mantinia styles marked by freshness and perfume.

name: Pedro Ximénez
description: The sherry grape behind the world's darkest dessert wine, sun-dried on mats until its juice pours like syrup. Solera-aged PX layers fig, raisin and coffee depth over a texture closer to sauce than to wine.

name: Ribolla Gialla
description: A Friulian white with bright acidity and a citrus-and-flowers profile that turns golden and textural with skin contact. The orange-wine movement's Italian flagbearer, at home on the Slovenian border hills.

name: Savagnin
description: Jura's ancient white grape, famous for Vin Jaune aged for years under a veil of yeast into something nutty, saline and unforgettable. Vinified fresh it shows alpine tension and orchard fruit instead.

name: Touriga Franca
description: The Douro's most planted grape and the perfumed, supple counterpart to Touriga Nacional in Port blends. On its own it gives floral, blackberry-fruited reds with fine-grained structure.

name: Frappato
description: Sicily's brightest red: pale, perfumed and strawberry-fresh, often blended with Nero d'Avola in Cerasuolo di Vittoria. Serve it cool and it drinks like a Mediterranean answer to cru Beaujolais.

name: Garganega
description: The grape of Soave, giving dry whites of pear, almond and white blossom from volcanic hills east of Verona. Old vines and late picking can push it from easy aperitif to genuinely age-worthy.

name: Graciano
description: Rioja's seasoning grape: low-yielding, intensely aromatic, and prized for the acidity and violet lift it brings to Tempranillo blends. Varietal bottlings are rare, inky and built to age.

name: Greco
description: An ancient Campanian white, at its peak in Greco di Tufo: stony, peachy and firm, with more grip than most Italian whites. Volcanic soils give it the smoky mineral spine it is known for.

name: Grillo
description: Sicily's sun-proof white, once the backbone of Marsala and now the island's crisp, grapefruit-and-jasmine seafood wine. It keeps its acidity in serious heat, which is exactly the point.

name: Hárslevelű
description: Tokaj's second grape, the linden-scented partner to Furmint in Aszú blends, adding honeyed perfume and spice to the world's oldest classified sweet wine. Dry versions are broad, floral and quietly serious.

name: Lambrusco
description: Emilia's family of sparkling red grapes, frothing violet-scented and sour-cherry dry — the real thing is a world away from the sweet export cliché. Built for a table loaded with cured pork and Parmigiano.

name: Loureiro
description: The laurel-scented white of Vinho Verde's Lima valley, all citrus blossom, bay leaf and Atlantic salt. Once a blending grape, it increasingly stands alone as Portugal's most fragrant light white.

name: Negroamaro
description: Puglia's 'black and bitter' grape, though the wines are more plush than the name warns: dark cherry, dried herbs and a savory, faintly saline finish. The backbone of Salice Salentino.

name: Poulsard
description: A ghost-pale Jura red with barely more pigment than a rosé, trading power for perfume: pomegranate, rose and forest floor. Fragile in the vineyard, haunting in the glass.

name: Trousseau
description: The sturdier of Jura's two red grapes, giving translucent wines with red cherry, pepper and a woodland earthiness. Known as Bastardo in Portugal, where it quietly seasons Port and Madeira.

name: Vidal
description: A thick-skinned French hybrid that found its destiny frozen solid on Canadian vines: Vidal icewine pours apricot, honey and tropical fruit over electric acidity. Ontario's Niagara Peninsula is its world capital.

name: Chinuri
description: Kartli's high-valley white, picked late for sparkling wine and vinified fresh or in qvevri for the table. Green apple, meadow herbs and mountain-stream acidity are its signature.

name: Goruli Mtsvane
description: Kartli's own 'green' grape, distinct from Kakheti's Mtsvane, bringing quince, white flowers and stony freshness to still and sparkling wines alike. A quiet component of Georgia's best fizz.

name: Mtsvane
description: Kakheti's aromatic white, often married to Rkatsiteli in qvevri for perfume the sturdier grape lacks. Skin contact turns its peach and blossom into amber-toned tea and stone fruit.

name: Otskhanuri Sapere
description: Imereti's rare, deeply colored red, fermented in clay churi for wines of sour cherry bite, violet lift and wild-country earth. One of Georgia's oldest varieties, and one of its scarcest.

name: Tsolikouri
description: Western Georgia's workhorse white, brighter and leaner than Kakheti's amber giants, with pear, honeyed blossom and wet-stone minerality. Imereti's partial skin-contact style suits it perfectly.

name: Romorantin
description: The only grape of tiny Cour-Cheverny, planted in the Loire on the orders of François I five centuries ago and grown nowhere else on earth. Razor acidity mellows with age into waxy, honeyed whites of quiet distinction.

name: Pineau d'Aunis
description: A medieval Loire red once poured for Plantagenet kings, now a handful of hectares of peppery, kirsch-pale wine. Its white-pepper bite made it a darling of the natural-wine bar and nearly nobody else.

name: Vaccarèse
description: One of Châteauneuf-du-Pape's forgotten thirteen, kept alive by a few faithful estates for the floral lift it lends Grenache. Almost never seen alone; the silvery-brown wood gives it its other name.

name: Muscardin
description: The rarest of Châteauneuf's authorized varieties, down to a scatter of rows across the whole appellation. What survives contributes perfume and freshness — a ghost grape in one of the world's most famous blends.

name: Terret Noir
description: An old Languedoc vine that earned one of Châteauneuf's thirteen seats for the acidity and herbal snap it brings to sun-heavy blends. A rare varietal bottling drinks pale, brisk and wild.

name: Picardan
description: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's least-planted white, a discreet salted-lemon seasoning surviving on single rows kept for the appellation's honor. Even growers there admit to walking past it without noticing.

name: Picpoul
description: The 'lip-stinger' of the Languedoc coast, all screaming citrus and salt, built for oyster beds an hour away. Also one of Châteauneuf's thirteen, where its acidity is the blend's seasoning; Blanc, Gris and Noir are all one family.

name: Counoise
description: The southern Rhône's quiet seasoning grape, prized in Châteauneuf blends for plummy fruit, pepper and acidity that Grenache burns off. A few varietal bottlings show what the blenders have been hoarding.

name: Clairette
description: One of the Rhône's oldest whites, blossomy and low in acid, long used to soften and perfume southern blends. Alone it makes the feather-light sparkler Clairette de Die and dry whites that fade young and gracefully.

name: Bourboulenc
description: A late-ripening Mediterranean white threaded through the southern Rhône and Languedoc, bringing citrus and a saline snap to blends that would otherwise sag in the heat. La Clape is its one starring role.

name: Pelaverga
description: Verduno's own pale-ruby secret, a single village's grape making strawberry-and-white-pepper reds beside some of Barolo's grandest crus. A few dozen hectares exist; the locals seem happy to keep it that way.

name: Ruché
description: Castagnole Monferrato's aromatic red riddle: rose-petal perfume over dark cherry, from a grape legend says a monk carried over the Alps. One small DOCG guards essentially the world's entire supply.

name: Timorasso
description: Rescued from a few abandoned rows in the Colli Tortonesi, Piedmont's great lost white makes dense, mineral wines that age like fine Riesling. Local growers sell it under the old hill name Derthona.

name: Nascetta
description: The village of Novello's half-forgotten white, once vinified sweet for special occasions and revived dry only in the 1990s. Sage-edged and honeyed, it is the Langhe's lone native white grape.

name: Vespaiolo
description: Breganze's high-acid white, named for the wasps that mob its sugar-rich berries at harvest. Its greatest act is Torcolato, an amber dessert wine pressed from bunches hung to dry through the winter.

name: Pignolo
description: Friuli's sternest red, saved from two surviving vines against an abbey wall in the 1970s. Massively tannic and slow to come around, it rewards the decade of patience almost nobody grants it.

name: Sagrantino
description: Montefalco's ferocious red, holder of the highest tannin levels of any major grape, once made only as a sacramental sweet wine. Modern dry Sagrantino is an Umbrian monument: black fruit, tar and decades of life.

name: Grignolino
description: Piedmont's contrarian: a pale, nervy red with prominent tannin from its many pips — the name derives from dialect for them. Once the region's aristocratic pour before Barolo stole the table.

name: Pignoletto
description: Bologna's own frothy white from the Colli Bolognesi, almost always lightly sparkling and poured beside mortadella. Genetically Grechetto Gentile, but Emilia would never call it anything so Umbrian.

name: Schioppettino
description: A Friulian border red that 'crackles' on the tongue — the name says so — rescued by one village's petition after phylloxera nearly ended it. Blueberry and cracked pepper over silky, alpine-fresh structure.

name: Carricante
description: Etna's ancient white, grown up the volcano's eastern slope where a thousand metres of altitude keep its acidity electric. Salted citrus over black-ash minerality, and a decade of graceful aging in the best bottles.

name: Hondarrabi Zuri
description: The white grape of Txakoli, poured theatrically from height into tumblers along the Basque coast. Low alcohol, a prickle of spritz, and acidity that tastes like the Bay of Biscay smells.

name: Hondarrabi Beltza
description: The red of the Basque coast, mostly vinified into rosé-pink, faintly fizzy Txakoli or brisk, crunchy reds served cool. Grown on cliff terraces where the vineyards end in surf.

name: Xarel·lo
description: The backbone of Cava and the most structured of its trio, increasingly bottled alone as Catalonia's serious still white. Orchard fruit and fennel over the acidity and grip that let top Cava age for a decade.

name: Bobal
description: Spain's secret workhorse — long the country's second most planted red, almost none of it ever labeled. Old bush vines in Utiel-Requena now yield dark, licorice-edged wines at improbable prices.

name: Mencía
description: The perfumed red of Spain's misty northwest, remade in a generation from jug wine into Bierzo's graphite-edged answer to fine Burgundy. Old slate-slope vines give it its floral lift and mineral spine.

name: Trepat
description: Conca de Barberà's pale local red, long hidden inside rosé Cava and only recently trusted with its own label. Strawberry-bright, peppery and feather-light — Catalonia's quiet answer to Pinot.

name: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains
description: The oldest and finest of the Muscat family, the rare grape whose wine actually smells of the grape itself. Alsace dries it out, the southern Rhône fortifies it into golden dessert wines.

name: Grenache Blanc
description: The white workhorse of the southern Rhône and Roussillon: fleshy, low-acid and quietly herbal, the padding in countless white blends. Old vines and restraint turn it from filler into something waxy and serious.

name: Colombard
description: Gascony's crisp everyday white, once distilled into Armagnac and now poured young, cold and unapologetically simple. The point is refreshment — citrus, a green snap, and no homework.

name: Mondeuse
description: Savoie's peppery mountain red, deep-coloured and wiry, tasting of dark cherries rolled in cracked pepper. Alpine acidity keeps it fresh where valley reds would slump.

name: Négrette
description: The floral dark grape of Fronton, north of Toulouse, making supple violet-scented reds almost nowhere else on earth. Locals call it the wine of the city; the rest of the Southwest lets them keep it.

name: Jacquère
description: The featherweight white of Savoie's ski villages, grown under limestone peaks and drunk within sight of them. Barely-there alcohol, alpine herbs and a chalky snap — fondue's official rinse.

name: Cortese
description: The grape behind Gavi, Piedmont's coolly precise white — pale, citrus-edged and faintly bitter-almond at the finish. Built for the fish that arrives an hour from the Ligurian coast.

name: Arneis
description: Roero's 'little rascal', a white so tricky to grow that Piedmont nearly let it die out in the 1960s. Rescued, it makes pear-and-blossom wines with a soft almond tail — Nebbiolo country's gentler face.

name: Pecorino
description: Not the cheese: a sharp-boned mountain white from the Marche and Abruzzo, named for the sheep that grazed its hillsides. Nearly extinct by the 1980s, now the thinking drinker's Italian white — herbal, saline and firm.

name: Vernaccia
description: The white of San Gimignano's towers, praised by Dante and licensed as Italy's first DOC in 1966. Lean, mineral and lightly almond-bitter — a medieval wine that never needed modernising.

name: Catarratto
description: Sicily's most-planted grape, long boiled down anonymously for Marsala and vermouth, now bottled on its own terms. Sun-fed lemon and honeysuckle over a dry herbal base — the island in a glass.

name: Cesanese
description: Lazio's own red, grown in the hills southeast of Rome since imperial times and mostly drunk before it ever reaches the city gates. Cherry-fruited and softly spicy, with a rose note that sneaks up on the finish.

name: Airén
description: The quiet giant of La Mancha's endless plateau — for decades the most-planted wine grape on earth, and almost nobody outside Spain has heard of it. Neutral, drought-proof and honest; much of it becomes brandy, the rest an unfussy lunch white.

name: Macabeo
description: Rioja calls it Viura and makes its whites from it; Penedès calls it Macabeo and puts it in the Cava trio with Xarel·lo and Parellada. Mild apple-blossom freshness young, surprising nutty depth when oaked and forgotten in a cellar.

name: Parellada
description: The finesse of the Cava trio, grown highest on the Penedès slopes and picked first. On its own it is delicate to the point of whispering; in the blend it is the lift that keeps the bubbles elegant.

name: Garnacha Blanca
description: Grenache Blanc under its home flag: Spain's fleshy white Garnacha, at its grandest in Terra Alta's old bush vines and a quiet stiffener in white Rioja. Ripe pear and anise with real weight — sunshine you can pour.

name: Listán Negro
description: The volcanic red of the Canary Islands, trained in braided cordons across black ash fields that never knew phylloxera. Smoky raspberry and pepper on a light frame — pre-colonial Spanish wine, still alive offshore.

name: Treixadura
description: Ribeiro's aristocrat, the peach-and-blossom white of Galicia's oldest wine valley, usually leading a local field blend. Softer-spoken than neighbouring Albariño, and prouder of it.

name: Bordeaux
description: The world's most famous wine region, renowned for its prestigious blends of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot. Its classification system and château culture have set the standard for fine wine globally.

name: Burgundy
description: The spiritual home of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, where terroir is expressed with unmatched precision. Its complex hierarchy of vineyards spans from regional wines to legendary Grand Crus.

name: Champagne
description: The only region that can legally produce true Champagne, using the traditional method of secondary fermentation in bottle. Its chalky soils and cool climate create wines of exceptional finesse and elegance.

name: Rhône Valley
description: A sun-drenched region divided into the elegant Northern Rhône and the broader Southern Rhône. It produces powerful Syrahs in the north and rich GSM blends in the south.

name: Loire Valley
description: Known as the Garden of France, this diverse region stretches along the Loire River. It produces everything from crisp Sauvignon Blanc to age-worthy Chenin Blanc and elegant Cabernet Franc.

name: Alsace
description: A unique French region with Germanic influence, known for its aromatic white wines in distinctive tall bottles. The dry Rieslings and spicy Gewürztraminers are among France's finest whites.

name: Provence
description: The world's most famous rosé-producing region, blessed with Mediterranean sunshine and maritime breezes. Its pale, dry rosés have become synonymous with summer elegance.

name: Beaujolais
description: The home of Gamay grape, producing bright, fruity wines that range from simple Nouveau to age-worthy Cru wines. Its ten crus showcase the diversity possible from a single grape variety.

name: Languedoc
description: France's largest wine region, offering exceptional value and increasingly high quality wines. Once known for bulk wine, it now produces exciting reds from Mediterranean varieties.

name: Chablis
description: A northern outpost of Burgundy famous for mineral, unoaked Chardonnay that expresses pure chalky terroir. Its Grand Crus and Premier Crus are among the world's greatest white wines.

name: Sauternes
description: The world's most celebrated sweet wine region, where noble rot transforms Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc into liquid gold. Château d'Yquem leads this prestigious appellation.

name: Jura
description: A quirky French region known for its unique oxidative wines like Vin Jaune and distinctive local grapes. Its Savagnin and Poulsard wines offer flavors found nowhere else.

name: Napa Valley
description: America's most prestigious wine region, known for powerful Cabernet Sauvignon that rivals Bordeaux. Its combination of climate, terroir, and investment has created world-class wines.

name: Sonoma
description: Napa's diverse coastal neighbor, producing excellent wines from numerous varieties across varied microclimates. Its cooler sites excel with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
climateDescription: Pacific fog and breezes temper ripening.

name: Willamette Valley
description: Oregon's cool-climate paradise for Pinot Noir, producing elegant wines that rival Burgundy. Its diverse soil types and microclimates create wines of remarkable complexity.

name: Paso Robles
description: California's hub for Rhône varieties, producing bold Syrahs and GSM blends in a warm, inland climate. Its limestone soils add complexity to powerful, ripe wines.

name: Walla Walla
description: Washington State's premium wine valley, known for elegant Syrah and refined Cabernet Sauvignon. Its high desert climate produces wines of intense flavor and balance.

name: Santa Barbara
description: Cool-climate California wine country made famous by the film Sideways. Its transverse valleys channel ocean fog to create ideal conditions for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
climateDescription: Ocean-cooled valleys with strong diurnal shift.

name: Finger Lakes
description: New York State's premier wine region, producing world-class Riesling from steep lakeside vineyards. The deep lakes moderate the harsh climate to allow viticulture.

name: Lodi
description: California's treasure trove of old vine Zinfandel, some over 100 years old. These ancient vines produce concentrated, complex wines at excellent value.

name: Tuscany
description: Italy's most beloved wine region, where Sangiovese reigns supreme across varied terroirs. From Chianti to Brunello to Super Tuscans, it offers incredible diversity.

name: Piedmont
description: The home of Nebbiolo, producing Italy's greatest red wines including Barolo and Barbaresco. Its fog-shrouded hills also yield excellent Barbera and Moscato.

name: Veneto
description: Italy's most productive wine region, home to Prosecco, Amarone, and Soave. Its diverse wines range from light sparklers to powerful dried-grape reds.

name: Sicily
description: Italy's largest wine island, producing increasingly impressive wines from ancient native varieties. Volcanic Mount Etna has become a hotbed for elegant reds and mineral whites.

name: Campania
description: Southern Italy's jewel of ancient grape varieties grown on volcanic soils near Naples. Aglianico produces powerful reds while Fiano and Greco make distinctive whites.

name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
description: Italy's top region for premium white wines, bordering Slovenia and Austria. Its mineral-driven Friulano and aromatic Ribolla Gialla showcase northeastern elegance.

name: Alto Adige
description: A bilingual Italian-German region in the Alps producing fresh, aromatic white wines. Its steep mountain vineyards yield distinctive Pinot Grigio and Gewürztraminer.

name: Abruzzo
description: Central Italy's workhorse region, famous for value-driven Montepulciano d'Abruzzo. Its rustic, fruity reds offer excellent quality at accessible prices.

name: Puglia
description: The heel of Italy's boot, producing bold, fruity reds from Primitivo and Negroamaro. Once a source of blending wine, it now bottles excellent value wines.

name: Rioja
description: Spain's most famous wine region, known for Tempranillo-based wines aged in American oak. Its traditional wines offer vanilla and coconut notes alongside red fruit.

name: Ribera del Duero
description: High-altitude wine country producing powerful, concentrated Tempranillo wines. Its extreme climate creates bold wines with intense fruit and firm structure.

name: Priorat
description: A dramatic region of ancient slate soils producing intensely concentrated wines. Its Garnacha and Cariñena vines struggle in poor soil to yield powerful, mineral wines.

name: Rías Baixas
description: Spain's premier white wine region on the Atlantic coast of Galicia. Its Albariño wines show distinctive salinity and freshness from the maritime influence.

name: Rueda
description: Spain's answer to Sauvignon Blanc country, producing crisp, herbal whites from Verdejo. Its limestone soils and continental climate create refreshing wines.

name: Jerez
description: The birthplace of Sherry, producing unique fortified wines through solera aging. From dry Fino to sweet Pedro Ximénez, it offers unmatched complexity.

name: Douro
description: Portugal's great river valley, home to Port wine and increasingly impressive dry reds. Its terraced schist hillsides are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: Vinho Verde
description: Portugal's refreshing white wine region producing light, crisp wines with a slight spritz. Its cool, rainy climate creates wines perfect for seafood.

name: Mosel
description: Germany's most famous wine region, producing ethereal Rieslings from impossibly steep slate slopes. Its light, aromatic wines balance sweetness with electric acidity.

name: Rheingau
description: A historic German region where noble Riesling was first cultivated for dry wines. Its south-facing slopes along the Rhine produce full-bodied, age-worthy whites.

name: Wachau
description: Austria's most prestigious wine region along the Danube River, producing world-class Riesling and Grüner Veltliner. Its terraced vineyards date back centuries.

name: Barossa Valley
description: Australia's most famous wine region, home to century-old Shiraz vines producing powerful, rich wines. Its warm climate and ancient soils create wines of incredible concentration.

name: Margaret River
description: Western Australia's premium region producing Bordeaux-style blends and elegant Chardonnay. Its maritime climate creates wines of exceptional balance and refinement.

name: Marlborough
description: New Zealand's largest and most famous region, producing intensely aromatic Sauvignon Blanc. Its wines have redefined the grape worldwide with their pungent tropical character.

name: Central Otago
description: The world's southernmost wine region, producing exceptional Pinot Noir at high altitude. Its dramatic landscape yields wines of remarkable purity and intensity.

name: Mendoza
description: Argentina's wine heartland at the foot of the Andes, where high-altitude vineyards produce world-class Malbec. Its sunny days and cool nights create wines of intense color and flavor.

name: Maipo Valley
description: Chile's most prestigious wine valley, known for powerful Cabernet Sauvignon. Its proximity to Santiago and excellent terroir make it Chile's wine showcase.

name: Stellenbosch
description: South Africa's premier wine region, producing world-class Cabernet Sauvignon and unique Pinotage. Its mountain slopes and varied soils create wines of great diversity.

name: Santorini
description: A Greek island of volcanic vineyards producing intensely mineral Assyrtiko. Its ancient vines are trained in basket shapes to protect against fierce winds.

name: Tokaj
description: Hungary's legendary region producing Tokaji Aszú, one of the world's great sweet wines. Its botrytis-affected Furmint grapes create wines of extraordinary complexity.

name: Helan Mountain
description: China's flagship high-desert wine frontier in Ningxia, producing polished Bordeaux-style reds under dramatic rocky ridges.

name: Shangri-La
description: Sky-high vineyards perched along the Mekong in Yunnan, delivering perfumed reds with alpine freshness from ancient terraces.

name: Yamanashi
description: Japan's Kōshu Valley beneath Mount Fuji, home to delicate Koshu whites and experimental sparkling wines with pristine acidity.

name: Nashik
description: India's wine capital north of Mumbai, where breezy plateaus yield tropical-leaning whites and peppery Syrah.

name: Nandi Hills
description: Cooler Karnataka hill country that lends lift and spice to India's premium Syrah and Cabernet bottlings.

name: Swartland
description: Swartland's old bush vines and granite soils craft textured Chenin Blanc and soulful Rhône-style reds with minimal intervention.

name: Walker Bay
description: A cool, ocean-swept corner famed for Hemel-en-Aarde Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, delivering Burgundian elegance with South African sunshine.

name: Paarl & Franschhoek
description: Historic valleys east of Stellenbosch producing rich reds, fynbos-scented whites, and South Africa's marquee Cap Classique sparklers.

name: Kakheti
description: Georgia's eastern cradle of wine, famous for skin-contact amber wines and powerful Saperavi reds fermented in buried qvevri.

name: Kartli
description: Highland vineyards near Tbilisi yielding elegant sparkling Chinuri and balanced qvevri whites with alpine freshness.

name: Imereti
description: Western Georgia's humid hills where partial qvevri fermentations craft brighter, mineral-driven amber and red wines.

name: Burgenland
description: Austria's red-wine country along the Hungarian border, where the shallow Neusiedlersee stretches the season for Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt. Its warm slopes also hide some of Europe's great botrytis sweet wines.

name: Niederösterreich
description: Lower Austria, the country's largest wine region, wrapping the Danube valleys and the vast Weinviertel. Grüner Veltliner is the calling card, peppery from loess terraces and windswept plains alike.

name: Canary Islands
description: Volcanic Atlantic islands where ungrafted vines grow in black-ash hollows behind hand-built stone walls. Ancient varieties survive here that phylloxera erased from the mainland centuries ago.
climateDescription: Volcanic islands cooled by Atlantic trade winds.

name: Marche
description: Italy's Adriatic hill country, where Verdicchio makes some of the nation's most age-worthy whites in the Castelli di Jesi and Matelica zones. Montepulciano-based reds from Conero add the other color.

name: Peloponnese
description: The mountainous southern peninsula of Greece, from Nemea's Agiorgitiko valleys to Mantinia's high plateau of rose-scented Moschofilero. Ancient sites and modern cellars share the same slopes.

name: Nemea
description: Greece's most important red appellation, a ring of valleys in the northeast Peloponnese given entirely to Agiorgitiko. Altitude decides everything here, from juicy valley reds to firm hillside wines.

name: Naoussa
description: Xinomavro's stronghold on the slopes of Mount Vermio in Greek Macedonia, making pale, tannic, tomato-and-olive reds that age like Barolo. The comparison to Nebbiolo is earned, not flattering.

name: Amyndeon
description: Greece's highest and coolest appellation, on a lake-moderated plateau where Xinomavro turns bright, floral and fine-boned. The country's most convincing rosés and sparkling reds start here.
climateDescription: The highest, coolest vineyards in Greece.

name: Sardinia
description: A granite island with its own grape lexicon: Vermentino di Gallura on the windy north coast, old-vine Cannonau inland, Carignano in the sandy southwest. Isolation kept its traditions intact.

name: Trentino
description: Alpine northern Italy along the Adige, split between mountain whites and the native Teroldego on the gravelly Campo Rotaliano. Its metodo classico sparkling wines rival Franciacorta.

name: Valpolicella
description: The Veneto's cherry-red heartland north of Verona, where Corvina and Rondinella range from light and fresh to the dried-grape monuments of Amarone. Ripasso wines split the difference.

name: Emilia-Romagna
description: Italy's food belt between the Po and the Apennines, washing Parmigiano and prosciutto down with dry, foaming Lambrusco. Sangiovese di Romagna holds up the still-red end of the table.

name: Etna
description: Vineyards climb the active volcano to nearly a thousand metres, where Nerello Mascalese reads more like alpine Pinot than Sicilian red. Black ash soils and centenarian vines do the talking.
climateDescription: Altitude on the volcano trumps Sicilian latitude.

name: Collio
description: A crescent of border hills between Friuli and Slovenia, Italy's benchmark for structured, site-driven whites. Friulano and Ribolla Gialla lead, often with skin contact in the old style.

name: Shandong
description: China's maritime wine coast, where the Yantai peninsula hosts the country's oldest modern wineries and most of its production. Humid summers make canopy work the whole game.

name: Hebei
description: The vineyards ringing Beijing, from coastal Changli to the Huailai basin at altitude. A proving ground for Cabernet Gernischt and the base for much of China's everyday wine.

name: Franconia
description: Germany's Silvaner country along the Main, bottling dry, earthy whites in the squat round Bocksbeutel. Limestone and gypsum soils give the wines their savory, stony cast.

name: Rheinhessen
description: Germany's largest wine region, reinvented in a generation from bulk supplier to the engine room of the country's dry-Riesling avant-garde. Silvaner and Pinot varieties fill out the rolling hills.

name: Gaillac
description: One of France's oldest vineyards, planted by the Romans on the Tarn, and a refuge for grapes that exist nowhere else. Peppery Fer Servadou reds and lightly fizzy méthode ancestrale whites keep it distinct.

name: Hunter Valley
description: Australia's oldest wine region and its most counterintuitive: subtropical heat producing featherweight, unoaked Semillon that ages for decades. Earthy, medium-weight Shiraz is the red tradition.
climateDescription: Subtropical heat broken by afternoon sea breezes.

name: Madeira
description: The Atlantic island whose fortified wines are deliberately heated and oxidised into near-immortality — bottles from the 1700s still drink. Verdelho and its sibling varieties ladder from dry to sweet.

name: Bairrada
description: Atlantic Portugal's clay country, where thick-skinned Baga makes structured, high-acid reds that repay a decade of patience. Its sparkling wines quietly supply half the country's fizz.

name: Dão
description: A granite bowl ringed by mountains that shelter it from both ocean and interior extremes — Portugal's Burgundy, by elevation and temperament. Touriga Nacional and Baga give polished, pine-edged reds.

name: Tejo
description: Portugal's river-plain workhorse turned value champion, retraining its fertile flats toward Arinto whites and Touriga-led reds. The Tagus moderates what the inland sun overdoes.

name: Bucelas
description: A tiny chalk-hill enclave north of Lisbon making bone-dry, age-worthy Arinto since Shakespeare's day — his plays name its wine. Atlantic fog keeps the acidity razor-sharp.

name: Alentejo
description: The wide, cork-oak south of Portugal, where warm plains and clay-schist hills give generous, round reds led by Aragonez and Touriga Nacional. Ancient clay-pot talha wines predate the Romans.

name: Salta
description: Home to some of the highest vineyards on earth, with Cafayate's vines near 1,700 metres and outliers past 3,000. Intense sun and cold nights make Torrontés electric and Malbec ink-dark.
climateDescription: High-altitude desert: fierce sun, cold nights.

name: Valdeorras
description: Galicia's inland valley of slate and sunlight, the source of Spain's most mineral Godello. Old Roman gold mines gave it terraces; the grape's revival gave it a future.

name: Bierzo
description: A misty mountain pass between Galicia and Castile where old-vine Mencía and Godello grow on steep slate. Its village-level classification is Spain's closest thing to Burgundy's ladder.

name: Yamagata
description: Northern Honshu's orchard prefecture, whose cool basins and snowy winters suit Muscat Bailey A and European varieties alike. Cherries made it famous; wine is catching up.

name: Niagara Peninsula
description: Canada's icewine capital between Lake Ontario and the Niagara Escarpment, where Vidal and Riesling freeze on the vine for December picking at -8°C. The same lake effect ripens serious dry wine in summer.
climateDescription: Lake Ontario keeps deep winter freezes vine-safe.

name: Okanagan Valley
description: British Columbia's desert-lake corridor, running from Canada's only true desert in the south to glacial-cooled Riesling country in the north. A four-hundred-kilometre climate gradient in one valley.

name: Dalmatia
description: Croatia's island-studded Adriatic coast, the ancestral home of Zinfandel — local Tribidrag and Plavac Mali still grow on karst terraces above the sea. Sun-baked, salt-licked reds are the signature.

name: Dealu Mare
description: Romania's 'Big Hill' on the Carpathian foothills, the country's most serious red district since Roman Dacia. Bordeaux varieties and native Fetească Neagră share the sunny slopes.

name: Valais
description: Switzerland's high Rhône valley, where terraced vines climb past 1,100 metres under föhn-warmed Alpine sun. Pinot Noir and Gamay lead the reds; glacier-fed Chasselas defines the whites.
climateDescription: Alpine sun and föhn winds ripen Europe's highest vines.

name: Canelones
description: Uruguay's Atlantic-cooled clay heartland just north of Montevideo, where most of the nation's Tannat grows on small family estates. Humid ocean air gives the wines their freshness and bite.

name: Guerrouane
description: Morocco's principal appellation on the Atlas foothills near Meknès, where altitude cools old plantings of Rhône varieties. Gris de Guerrouane rosé is the country's best-known bottle.

name: Valle de Guadalupe
description: Baja California's granite valley two hours south of the border, cooled by Pacific fog and unbound by appellation rules. Nebbiolo, Tempranillo and inventive blends define Mexico's wine renaissance.
climateDescription: Pacific fog rolls into a dry granite valley.

name: Châteauneuf-du-Pape
description: The southern Rhône's crown, where thirteen authorized varieties grow among fist-sized galet stones below a ruined papal castle. Grenache leads the blend, but the appellation's fame rests on the whole chorus — including varieties nearly extinct everywhere else.
climateDescription: Round galet stones bank the day's heat into the night.

name: Umbria
description: Italy's green, landlocked heart, where Orvieto whites flow from tufa cliffs and Montefalco's Sagrantino makes the country's most tannic red. Hill towns and monastic cellars keep winemaking on a medieval clock.

name: Basque Country
description: Green cliff-top vineyards above the Bay of Biscay, where Hondarrabi Zuri and Beltza make Txakoli — low-alcohol, faintly fizzy, poured from a height into tumblers. Wine built for pintxos and salt air.
climateDescription: Atlantic mist keeps Txakoli country cool and green.

name: Penedès
description: Catalonia's Cava heartland between Barcelona and the sea, where Xarel·lo, Macabeo and Parellada ripen for the traditional method. The hills behind hold some of Spain's most experimental still cellars.

name: Utiel-Requena
description: A high inland plateau behind Valencia, planted to old bush-vine Bobal that survived a century of anonymity in bulk blends. The altitude's cold nights are turning the workhorse into a thoroughbred.

name: Conca de Barberà
description: A cool Catalan river basin ringed by monasteries, home ground of the pale red Trepat and a quiet supplier of rosé Cava. Modernist stone co-op cellars — 'wine cathedrals' — still work its harvest.

name: Corsica
description: France's mountain island, closer to Italy in miles and grape names alike. Granite hills over a turquoise sea grow herbal reds and salt-edged Vermentino under maquis-scented air.
climateDescription: An island climate: sea on every side, mountains up the middle.

name: Savoie
description: Ski-country vineyards strung beneath the French Alps, growing whites of glacial clarity and the peppery red Mondeuse. Most of it is drunk within sight of the slopes it grew on.
climateDescription: Alpine valleys where altitude does what latitude cannot.

name: Roussillon
description: The Catalan corner of France, an amphitheatre of windswept terraces dropping from the Pyrenees to the Mediterranean. Old-vine Grenache in every colour, plus the fortified sweet wines the region built its name on.

name: Cahors
description: The original home of Malbec, making 'black wine' on the Lot's limestone terraces centuries before Argentina borrowed the grape. Sterner and earthier than its South American offspring, and proud of the difference.

name: Lombardy
description: Milan's home region, quietly making Italy's most serious traditional-method sparkling in Franciacorta and alpine Nebbiolo in Valtellina's terraced north. Industrial money, mountain wine.

name: Lazio
description: Rome's countryside, pouring the capital's carafe whites from the Castelli hills since antiquity — and lately rediscovering Cesanese, its own spicy red. Two thousand years of thirsty customers, finally some ambition.

name: Calabria
description: The toe of the boot, where Greek settlers planted vines twenty-seven centuries ago and Cirò still grows on the same coastal shelf. Sun-baked reds and a long memory, far from the wine world's spotlight.

name: Basilicata
description: One grape, one volcano: Aglianico del Vulture grows in black ash on the slopes of a long-dead cone, ripening later than almost anything in Italy. Small, poor, and pound for pound one of the south's greatest reds.
climateDescription: High vineyards on an extinct volcano temper the southern heat.

name: Toro
description: Castile's bruiser: pre-phylloxera Tempranillo — here called Tinta de Toro — on sandy plains that the louse never conquered. Wines of massive colour and grip that Madrid's restaurants treat as a birthright.

name: Navarra
description: Pilgrim country on the road to Santiago, long Spain's rosado capital and now an open workshop where Garnacha old-timers share terraces with international grapes. Forever in Rioja's shadow, rarely in its price bracket.

name: La Mancha
description: Don Quixote's plateau, the largest vine planting on earth — a sea of Airén stretching past every horizon south of Madrid. Long the continent's brandy tank, now quietly Europe's biggest source of honest cheap wine.

name: Ribeira Sacra
description: The 'sacred riverbank': Roman terraces stacked up canyon walls so steep the harvest comes down by boat and pulley. Mencía grown here tastes of slate, river fog and the nerve of whoever picked it.
climateDescription: Atlantic air funnels up the canyons of the Sil and Miño.

name: Full-Body Red
description: Rich, tannic wines with intense dark fruit flavors that command attention on the palate. These powerful wines typically benefit from aging and pair beautifully with hearty red meats.

name: Light-Body Red
description: Delicate, elegant reds with bright acidity and fresh red fruit character that are perfect for lighter fare. These subtle wines showcase finesse over power and can even be served slightly chilled.

name: Medium-Body Red
description: Versatile reds that balance fruit, structure, and elegance for everyday enjoyment. These food-friendly wines bridge the gap between light and bold styles.

name: Full-Body White
description: Opulent white wines often with oak influence, offering rich texture and creamy mouthfeel. These wines pair wonderfully with rich seafood, poultry, and cream-based dishes.

name: Light-Body White
description: Crisp, refreshing whites with high acidity and clean, mineral-driven flavors. These thirst-quenching wines are perfect aperitifs or paired with light seafood.

name: Aromatic White
description: Intensely fragrant white wines with floral, fruity, and spicy aromas that leap from the glass. These expressive wines often have a touch of residual sugar to balance their bold aromatics.

name: Rosé
description: Refreshing pink wines made from red grapes with minimal skin contact. These versatile, food-friendly wines range from bone-dry to slightly sweet.

name: Sparkling Wine
description: Effervescent wines with elegant bubbles created through secondary fermentation. From simple Prosecco to prestigious Champagne, bubbles add celebration to any occasion.

name: Champagne
description: The original and most prestigious sparkling wine, made only in the Champagne region of France. Its traditional method production creates unmatched finesse and complexity.

name: Dessert Wine
description: Lusciously sweet wines crafted from super-ripe or dried grapes, perfect for ending a meal. These concentrated wines balance intense sweetness with vibrant acidity.

name: Fortified Wine
description: Wines strengthened with grape spirit to increase alcohol and preserve sweetness. From dry Sherry to sweet Port, these complex wines offer remarkable longevity.

name: Port
description: Portugal's famous sweet fortified wine from the Douro Valley, made by adding brandy during fermentation. Its rich, concentrated flavors range from fruity Ruby to aged Tawny styles.

name: Sherry
description: Spain's unique fortified wine from Jerez, aged in a solera system to create complex oxidative or biological styles. From dry Fino to sweet Pedro Ximénez, it offers incredible diversity.

name: Natural Wine
description: Low-intervention wines made with minimal additives and often without filtration. These authentic wines showcase the true expression of grape and terroir.

name: Orange Wine
description: White grapes vinified like red wine, with extended skin contact creating amber color and tannic structure. This ancient technique produces textural, complex wines.

name: Pétillant Naturel
description: Naturally sparkling wines made using the ancestral method, bottled before primary fermentation completes. These rustic, cloudy sparklers offer fresh, unpredictable character.

name: Late Harvest
description: Sweet wines made from grapes left on the vine past normal harvest to concentrate sugar. This simple technique creates rich, fruity dessert wines without noble rot.

name: Ice Wine
description: Ultra-sweet wines made from grapes naturally frozen on the vine, concentrating sugars and acids. These rare, expensive wines require specific climate conditions to produce.

name: Botrytis Wine
description: Noble rot sweet wines where Botrytis cinerea fungus concentrates grape sugars while adding honeyed complexity. Sauternes and Tokaji are the most famous examples.

name: GSM Blend
description: Classic Rhône-style blend of Grenache, Syrah, and Mourvèdre creating complex, balanced reds. Each grape contributes fruit, structure, and aromatics to the final wine.

name: Bordeaux Blend
description: Classic blend dominated by Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot with supporting varieties. This noble style has been replicated worldwide for its structure and aging potential.

name: Super Tuscan
description: Non-traditional Italian wines that broke from DOC rules by blending international varieties with local grapes. These innovative wines put modern Italian winemaking on the map.

name: Cru Beaujolais
description: Age-worthy Gamay from the ten named villages of Beaujolais, offering serious wines beyond simple Nouveau. Each cru has distinct character from its unique granite-based terroir.

name: Crémant
description: French sparkling wines made in the traditional method outside Champagne, offering excellent value. Crémant d'Alsace, Loire, and Burgundy are the most notable examples.

name: Prosecco
description: Italy's most popular sparkling wine, made from Glera grapes using the tank method. Its fresh, fruity character and gentle bubbles make it perfect for casual celebrations.

name: Qvevri Amber
description: Skin-contact whites fermented in buried clay qvevri, yielding tea-like tannin, dried orchard fruit, and honeyed spice.

name: Chillable Red
description: Light, low-tannin reds built for a chill, bursting with red fruit and peppery zest for warm-weather sipping.

name: Sparkling Red
description: Fizz meets dark fruit: from Lambrusco to sparkling Shiraz, these wines marry bubbles with berry-rich, savory depth.

name: Noble Grapes
description: A curated grouping of the NOBLE-tier varieties whose pedigree, structure, and complexity define the most prestigious styles.

name: Medium-Body White
description: White wines with real texture but no oak heaviness, sitting between crisp aperitif and full-blown richness. Their weight comes from the grape and the lees rather than the barrel, which keeps them versatile at the table.

name: Sweet White
description: Unabashedly sweet whites, from gently fizzy Moscato to syrup-dark Pedro Ximénez and frozen-vine Vidal icewine. The best balance their sugar with enough acidity or perfume that the last glass is as welcome as the first.

name: Blackcurrant
description: Blackcurrant is a ripe, sweet-leaning berry note — it reads as ripeness first, the sort of aroma that promises fruit before the sip.

name: Cedar
description: Cedar is a savoury, umami-leaning wood note — it sits under the fruit as a savoury depth, closer to a place or a pantry than an orchard.

name: Spice
description: Spice is a firm, bitter-edged note — it shows as grip and edge on the finish more than as a smell.

name: Cherry
description: Cherry is a ripe, sweet-leaning red fruit note — it reads as ripeness first, the sort of aroma that promises fruit before the sip.

name: Earth
description: Earth is a savoury, umami-leaning note — it sits under the fruit as a savoury depth, closer to a place or a pantry than an orchard.

name: Floral
description: Floral is a savoury, umami-leaning note — it sits under the fruit as a savoury depth, closer to a place or a pantry than an orchard.

name: Red Apple
description: Red Apple is a ripe, sweet-leaning orchard fruit note — it reads as ripeness first, the sort of aroma that promises fruit before the sip.

name: Butter
description: Butter is a ripe, sweet-leaning baking note — it reads as ripeness first, the sort of aroma that promises fruit before the sip.

name: Vanilla
description: Vanilla is a ripe, sweet-leaning baking note — it reads as ripeness first, the sort of aroma that promises fruit before the sip.

name: Plum
description: Plum is a ripe, sweet-leaning dark fruit note — it reads as ripeness first, the sort of aroma that promises fruit before the sip.

name: Chocolate

name: North America
description: The birthplace of New World wine, North America combines Old World traditions with innovative winemaking. From California's sun-drenched valleys to Canada's cool-climate vineyards, the continent produces a diverse range of styles that have revolutionized global wine production.

name: Europe
description: The cradle of viticulture, Europe has shaped wine culture for millennia. From France's prestigious appellations to Italy's ancient vineyards, Europe's diverse climates and terroirs produce wines of unparalleled complexity and tradition.

name: Asia
description: An emerging wine frontier blending ancient traditions with modern innovation. From China's high-altitude vineyards to Japan's delicate whites, Asia's diverse landscapes are producing increasingly sophisticated wines that reflect both heritage and contemporary winemaking.

name: South America
description: A continent of extremes, from Andean foothills to coastal plains, producing bold, expressive wines. Argentina's Malbec and Chile's Cabernet Sauvignon have become global benchmarks for value and quality in the New World.

name: Africa
description: Africa's wine heritage spans from ancient Egyptian traditions to modern innovations. South Africa's Cape region produces world-class wines that blend Old World elegance with New World vibrancy, while other regions are rapidly developing their vinicultural potential.

name: Oceania
description: The southernmost wine regions of the world, where maritime climates and diverse terroirs create distinctive wines. Australia's bold Shiraz and New Zealand's aromatic Sauvignon Blanc have redefined international wine styles.
